t:
Section 4 of Public Law 90–275 (82 Stat. 68) is amended to read as follows:


“Sec. 4. 
The annual income limitations governing payment of pension under the first sentence of section 9(b) of the Veterans’ Pension Act of 1959 hereafter shall be $2,200 and $3,500, instead of $1,900 and $3,200, respectively.”

fable.w: This section only amends the dollar thresholds for income limitations governing veterans' pension payments. There is no tempting reading here beyond the fact that it concerns benefits for members of the public; it involves no consultation, hearing, rulemaking, advisory body, or right to sue, and no outside party takes part in any federal decision.
fable.s: The annual income limitations governing payment of pension under the first sentence of section 9(b) of the Veterans’ Pension Act of 1959 hereafter shall be $2,200 and $3,500, instead of $1,900 and $3,200, respectively.

opus.w: The section only replaces the pension income limits of $1,900 and $3,200 with $2,200 and $3,500. It does not have any federal decision-maker consult or coordinate with anyone outside the government. The pension link to veterans is a benefits matter, and benefits are excluded from participation under the definition.
opus.b: Step 1: Someone might read "pension" as a benefits program that involves outside parties. But the section only changes the dollar amounts of the income limits for veterans' pensions. It sets up no consultation, hearing, comment period, advisory body, rulemaking authority or right to sue. Applications for benefits would not count as participation anyway.

qwen_chat.w: This section simply amends the statutory dollar amounts for pension income limitations. It does not require the federal government to consult, coordinate with, or seek input from any outside parties (such as veterans, states, or the public) before making this decision. The definition of participation requires interaction with outside parties, whereas this is a unilateral legislative determination of benefit levels.
qwen_chat.s: The annual income limitations governing payment of pension under the first sentence of section 9(b) of the Veterans’ Pension Act of 1959 hereafter shall be $2,200 and $3,500, instead of $1,900 and $3,200, respectively.
qwen_chat.b: Tempting-but-wrong reading: One might argue that changing pension limits affects veterans (outside the government), so it involves them. However, the definition explicitly excludes "applications for benefits or grants" and requires active consultation, coordination, or decision-making input from outside parties. This section merely sets a statutory dollar amount; it does not require the government to consult with veterans or any other outside group before setting that amount.
